arxiv-1810-06748.title: Assessing the Contribution of Semantic Congruency to Multisensory Integration and Conflict Resolution Thanks: Knowledge Technology, Department of Informatics, Universität Hamburg, Germany. {surname}@informatik.uni-hamburg.de Thanks: CAS Key Laboratory of Behavioral Science, Chinese Academy of Scienc
arxiv-1810-06748.description: Abstract The efficient integration of multisensory observations is a key property of the brain that yields the robust interaction with the environment. However, artificial multisensory perception remains an open issue especially in situations of sensory uncertainty and conflicts. In this work, we extend previous studies on audio-visual (AV) conflict resolution in complex environments.

arxiv-2206-11023.title: Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks for Software Effort Estimation Conference: ACM / IEEE International Symposium on Empirical Software Engineering and Measurement (ESEM); September 19–23, 2022; Helsinki, Finland ACM / IEEE International Symposium on Empirical Software Engineering and Measurement (E
arxiv-2206-11023.creator: Hung Phan, Ali Jannesari
arxiv-2206-11023.description: Abstract . Background. Software effort can be measured by story point ( Usman et al. 2014 ) . Story point estimation is important in software projects’ planning. Current approaches for automatically estimating story points focus on applying pre-trained embedding models and deep learning for text regression to solve this problem.

arxiv-2210-03551.title: Instance Segmentation of Dense and Overlapping Objects via Layering
arxiv-2210-03551.creator: Long Chen, Yuli Wu, Dorit Merhof
arxiv-2210-03551.description: Abstract Instance segmentation aims to delineate each individual object of interest in an image. State-of-the-art approaches achieve this goal by either partitioning semantic segmentations or refining coarse representations of detected objects. In this work, we propose a novel approach to solve the problem via object layering, i.e. by distributing crowded, even overlapping objects into different layers.

arxiv-2304-00659.title: Thermodynamic engine with a quantum degenerate working fluid
arxiv-2304-00659.creator: Ethan Q. Simmons, Roshan Sajjad, Kimberlee Keithley, Hector Mas, Jeremy L. Tanlimco, Eber Nolasco-Martinez, Yifei Bai, Glenn H. Fredrickson, David M. Weld
arxiv-2304-00659.description: Abstract Can quantum mechanical thermodynamic engines outperform their classical counterparts? To address one aspect of this question, we experimentally realize and characterize an isentropic thermodynamic engine that uses a Bose-condensed working fluid. In this engine, an interacting quantum degenerate gas of bosonic lithium is subjected to trap compression and relaxation strokes interleaved with strokes strengthening and weakening interparticle interactions.

arxiv-2305-01954.title: SeqAug: Sequential Feature Resampling as a modality agnostic augmentation method
arxiv-2305-01954.creator: Efthymios Georgiou 1,2 , Alexandros Potamianos 2
arxiv-2305-01954.description: Abstract Data augmentation is a prevalent technique for improving performance in various machine learning applications. We propose SeqAug, a modality-agnostic augmentation method that is tailored towards sequences of extracted features. The core idea of SeqAug is to augment the sequence by resampling from the underlying feature distribution.

arxiv-2311-07443.title: Renormalization group improved photon impact factors and the high energy virtual photon scattering
arxiv-2311-07443.creator: Dimitri Colferai, Wanchen Li, Anna M. Staśto
arxiv-2311-07443.description: Abstract We perform the renormalization group improved collinear resummation of the photon-gluon impact factors. We construct the resummed cross section for virtual photon-photon ( γ ∗ ​ γ ∗ \gamma^{*}\gamma^{*} ) scattering which incorporates the impact factors and BFKL gluon Green’s function up to the next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy in energy.

arxiv-2404-01178.title: Projective contact log varieties
arxiv-2404-01178.creator: Adrian Langer
arxiv-2404-01178.description: Abstract We study contact structures on smooth complex projective varieties with a simple normal crossing divisor, generalizing some well-known results concerning the non-logarithmic case. In particular, we describe the structure of elementary log contractions of such log varieties and we construct the corresponding contact structures. Address: Institute of Mathematics, University of Warsaw, ul. Banacha 2, 02-097 Warszawa, Poland e-mail: alan@mimuw.edu.

arxiv-2404-14891.title: Equivalence Relations in Quantum Theory: An Objective Account of Bases and Factorizations .
arxiv-2404-14891.creator: Christian de Ronde, Raimundo Fernández Mouján, César Massri
arxiv-2404-14891.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Christian de Ronde, Raimundo Fernández Mouján, César Massri. In orthodox Standard Quantum Mechanics (SQM) bases and factorizations are considered to define quantum states and entanglement in relativistic terms. While the choice of a basis (interpreted as a measurement context) defines a state incompatible to that same state in a different basis, the choice of a factorization (interpreted as the separability of systems into sub-systems) determines wether the same state is entangled or non-entangled.

arxiv-2408-04403.title: Exploring Reasoning Biases in Large Language Models Through Syllogism: Insights from the NeuBAROCO Dataset
arxiv-2408-04403.creator: Kentaro Ozeki, Risako Ando, Takanobu Morishita, Hirohiko Abe, Koji Mineshima, Mitsuhiro Okada
arxiv-2408-04403.description: Abstract This paper explores the question of how accurately current large language models can perform logical reasoning in natural language, with an emphasis on whether these models exhibit reasoning biases similar to humans. Specifically, our study focuses on syllogistic reasoning, a form of deductive reasoning extensively studied in cognitive science as a natural form of human reasoning.

arxiv-2511-22417.title: Design of Cycles by Impulsive Feedback: Application to Discrete Dosing
arxiv-2511-22417.creator: Alexander Medvedev, Anton V. Proskurnikov, Zhanybai T. Zhusubaliyev
arxiv-2511-22417.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alexander Medvedev, Anton V. Proskurnikov, Zhanybai T. Zhusubaliyev. The task of maintaining a predefined level of effect in a dynamical plant by applying periodic control actions often arises in e.g. process control and medicine. When the state variables of the plant represent the concentrations of chemical substances and the control action constitutes an instantaneous introduction of a certain quantity of a chemical or drug, this control setup is referred to as a (discrete) dosing problem.

pmc-10541704.title: Influenza H7N9 virus disrupts the monolayer human brain microvascular endothelial cells barrier in vitro
pmc-10541704.creator: Yuxuan Lei, Ying Sun, Weihua Wu, Hui Liu, Xin Wang, Yuelong Shu, Shisong Fang
pmc-10541704.description: Influenza H7N9 virus causes human infections with about 40% case fatality rate. The severe cases usually present with pneumonia; however, some present with central nervous system complications. Pneumonia syndrome is attributed to the cytokine storm after infection with H7N9, but the pathogenic mechanism of central nervous system complications has not been clarified.

pmc-10625884.title: Effect of artificial aging on mechanical and physical properties of CAD-CAM PMMA resins for occlusal splints
pmc-10625884.creator: Júlia Correa Raffaini, Eduardo Jose Soares, Rebeca Franco de Lima Oliveira, Rocio Geng Vivanco, Ayodele Alves Amorim, Ana Lucia Caetano Pereira, Fernanda Carvalho Panzeri Pires-de-Souza
pmc-10625884.description: PURPOSEThis study aimed to assess and compare the color stability, flexural strength (FS), and surface roughness of occlusal splints fabricated from heat-cured acrylic resin, milled polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA)-based resin, and 3D-printed (PMMA) based-resin.MATERIALS AND METHODSSamples of each type of resin were obtained, and baseline measurements of color and surface roughness were recorded.

pmc-11312875.title: Identification of a Human Trafficking Victim: A Simulation
pmc-11312875.creator: Claire A Grosgogeat, Kelly Medwid, Rami H Mahmoud, Brooke Hensley
pmc-11312875.description: AudienceThis case was designed for emergency medicine interns and residents.IntroductionHuman trafficking is unfortunately an ever-growing and wide-reaching problem in the United States as well as the rest of the world. The International Labor Organization estimates 49.6 million people were affected by this modern-day slavery worldwide in 2021.

pmc-11451048.title: Neurodegenerative diseases reflect the reciprocal roles played by retroelements in regulating memory and immunity
pmc-11451048.creator: Alan Herbert
pmc-11451048.description: Tetrapod endogenous retroelements (ERE) encode proteins that have been exapted to perform many roles in development and also in innate immunity, including GAG (group specific antigen) proteins from the ERE long terminal repeat (LTR) family, some of which can assemble into viral-like capsids (VLCs) and transmit mRNA across synapses.

pmc-11557355.title: Case report: Primary cytomegalovirus infection in a patient with late onset multiple sclerosis treated with dimethyl fumarate
pmc-11557355.creator: Julia Sabin Muñoz, Alberto Díaz-De Santiago, José Cebrián Escudero, J. A. García Merino
pmc-11557355.description: BackgroundTreatment of multiple sclerosis (MS) with delayed-release dimethyl fumarate (DMF) has shown efficacy and safety in clinical trials. However, the occurrence of infectious complications, particularly in elderly patients, remains a concern.MethodsWe present the case of a 63-year-old woman with late-onset MS treated with DMF, who developed a severe primary cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection.

pmc-11600710.title: Factors influencing provider deviation from national HIV and nutritional guidelines for HIV-exposed children in western Kenya: a qualitative study
pmc-11600710.creator: Megan M Coe, Emily Yoshioka, Damaris Odhiambo, Mary Masheti, Phlona Amam, Julius Nyaoke, Emmanuel Oduor, Marline Serede, Agnes Ndirangu, Benson Singa, Arianna Rubin Means
pmc-11600710.description: BackgroundMalnutrition and HIV interact in a vicious cycle for HIV-exposed infants (HEIs), increasing vulnerability and the severity of each condition and contributing to poor health outcomes. We identified multi-level factors influencing provider adherence to Kenyan HIV and nutrition guidelines for HEIs.MethodsWe conducted six focus group discussions and seven in-depth interviews using a semi-structured question guide.

pmc-12510036.title: Epidemiological trends and burden of mortality from HIV/AIDS and multidrug-resistant tuberculosis without extensive drug-resistance across Africa: A global burden of disease analysis (1990–2021)
pmc-12510036.creator: Ibrahim Khalil, Noshin Anjum Tasmi, MdImran Hossain, MstMahmuda Akter
pmc-12510036.description: Highlights•HIV/AIDS & MDR-TB mortality surged in 1990s, declined post-2003 in Africa.•Central Africa saw steepest decline (APC: −15.75 %, 2016–2021) due to ART.•Northern Africa showed rising trend (AAPC: 3.56 %, p = 0.014) in mortality.•Females had steeper declines than males, driven by PMTCT programs.•Southern Africa’s high HIV burden persists, with slower declines post-2014.

pmc-13347233.creator: Akinyemi Oni‐Orisan
pmc-13347233.description: I anchor the discussion around preventing adverse drug events. Future endeavors that advance both fields together will enable comprehensive achievement of improved pharmacotherapeutic health outcomes for all. Adverse drug events Over the past several decades, the widespread use of prescription drugs has contributed to improved life expectancy for the over 200 million Americans who receive them yearly.

pmc-13555867.title: Cardioprotective effects of right stellate ganglion block combined with dexmedetomidine in rats with atrial fibrillation-like atrial tachyarrhythmia
pmc-13555867.creator: Renhao Xu, Jin Zhang, Qiongmei Guo, Deli Zheng, Xiangjian Zhang, Li Wang
pmc-13555867.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate right stellate ganglion block (SGB) plus dexmedetomidine (Dex) in a rat model of atrial fibrillation-like (AF-like) atrial tachyarrhythmia. Methods: Male Sprague-Dawley rats were assigned to Sham, AF, AF+amiodarone, AF + SGB and AF + SGB+Dex groups. AF-like atrial tachyarrhythmia was induced by daily CaCl₂-acetylcholine injections for 7 days, and interventions were administered 1 h before modelling.

pmc-13653169.title: Non-Ultrasound-Guided Versus Ultrasound-Guided Femoral Venous Puncture in the Interventional Pulmonary Embolism Era: Does Ultrasound Guidance Improve Safety and Feasibility?
pmc-13653169.creator: Abdelrahman Elhakim, Desouki Abdelatti, Mohamed Elhakim, Osama Bisht, Ibrahim Yassin, Mohamed A Mosaad, Ahmad M Hassaan, Peter W. Radke, Mohammed Saad
pmc-13653169.description: Background:The use of interventional endovascular therapy for pulmonary embolism (PE) has become increasingly important over the last decade. In contrast to other cardiovascular interventions, these procedures carry a higher risk of access-related bleeding due to the acute clinical setting, elevated body mass index, and the frequent need for high-dose anticoagulation.
